item.content:encoded:
USS George Washington (CVN-73) left the Middle East after being on station for three months, a U.S. Pacific Fleet spokesperson confirmed Wednesday to USNI News. 

George Washington is now in U.S. 7th Fleet. The spokesperson did not provide additional details, including which of George Washington’s escorts accompanied the ship.

George Washington and its escorts USS Robert Smalls (CG-62) and destroyer USS Shoup (DDG-86) arrived in U.S. 5th Fleet on Aug. 19, USNI News previously reported. The Japan-based carrier strike group, originally out on a western Pacific deployment, headed to the Middle East to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-71) and some of its escorts.

George Washington and Lincoln overlapped for a few days before Lincoln departed for home. Similarly, the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group arrived in the Middle East on Sunday prior to George Washington’s departure. The George H.W. Bush Carrier Strike Group has been in the Arabian Sea since April, making three carrier strike groups in the Middle East for a couple of days during each overlap, according to USNI News’ Fleet and Marine Tracker. 

With George Washington now in the Indian Ocean, there are two carrier strike groups in the Middle East. 

It is unclear whether George Washington is heading home or if the carrier will make a port call as it heads east. The aircraft carrier deployed in late May from Yokosuka, Japan, for its spring patrol. 

Before being sent to the Middle East, George Washington made port calls in Vietnam and Guam, as well as conducted patrols in the Philippine Sea. The order to relieve Lincoln in the Middle East left the U.S. without a carrier in the Indo-Pacific region. 

Families of sailors have raised concerns about extended deployments and conditions on ships, particularly Lincoln and George H.W. Bush (CVN-77). The latter may see a year-long deployment, breaking records held by USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) and Lincoln. 

Destroyers attached to the aircraft carriers are also seeing longer deployments, often extending past the carrier’s deployment. USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) and USS Spruance (DDG-111) just returned home after 346 days and 357 days deployed, respectively. Spruance’s deployment lasted 36 days more than Lincoln’s.

These are the approximate positions of the U.S. Navy’s deployed carrier strike groups and amphibious ready groups throughout the world as of Nov. 16, 2026, based on Navy and public data. In cases in which a CSG or ARG is conducting disaggregated operations, the chart reflects the location of the capital ship.

In Japan

USS Tripoli (LHA-7) is in port in Sasebo, Japan.

In the Philippine Sea

Amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) is underway conducting routine operations in the Philippine Sea.

The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group includes Makin Island, USS Anchorage (LPD-23), USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) and the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit.

In the Caribbean Sea

Littoral combat ship USS Minneapolis-Saint Paul (LCS-21) is operating in the central Caribbean Sea. The Freedom-class LCS is based at Naval Station Mayport, Fla.

In the Mediterranean Sea

The independently deployed guided-missile destroyers operating in the Mediterranean Sea include:

  • USS Oscar Austin (DDG-79), homeported at Naval Station Rota.
  • USS Bulkeley (DDG-84), homeported at Naval Station Rota.
  • USS Paul Ignatius (DDG-117), homeported at Naval Station Rota.
  • USS Stout (DDG-55), homeported at Naval Station Norfolk, Va.

Command ship, USS Mount Whitney (LCC-20) was observed Friday in Piraeus, Greece, according to ship spotters. The ship completed the port visit on Sunday, reads a Navy news release.

In the Red Sea

There are two guided-missile destroyers operating in the Red Sea:

  • USS Jason Dunham (DDG-109), homeported at Naval Station Mayport, Fla.
  • USS Gonzalez (DDG-66), homeported at Naval Station Norfolk, Va.

In the Arabian Sea

Aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN-73), along with embarked Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 5 and USS Shoup (DDG-86), are operating in the Arabian Sea in support of U.S. operations in the Middle East.

Carrier Strike Group 5

Carrier
USS George Washington (CVN-73), homeported in Yokosuka, Japan.

Carrier Air Wing 5

  • The “Royal Maces” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 27 – F/A-18E – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni, Japan.
  • The “Diamondbacks” of VFA 102 – F/A-18F – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Argonauts” of VFA 147 – F-35C – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Dambusters” of VFA 195 – F/A-18E – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Shadowhawks” of Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 141 – EA-18G – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Tigertails” of Airborne Command and Control Squadron (VAW) 125 – E-2D – from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Titans” of Fleet Logistics Multi-Mission Squadron (VRM) 30 Det 5 — CMV-22B — from Marine Corps Air Station, Iwakuni.
  • The “Saberhawks” of Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 77 – MH-60R — from Naval Air Facility, Atsugi, Japan.
  • The “Golden Falcons” of Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 12 – MH 60S — from Naval Air Facility, Atsugi.

Destroyer Squadron 15

Destroyer Squadron 15 is based in Yokosuka, Japan, and embarked aboard George Washington.

  • USS Shoup (DDG-86), homeported in Yokosuka.
  • USS Ross (DDG-71), homeported at Naval Station Norfolk, Va.

The George H.W. Bush Carrier Strike Group is operating in the Arabian Sea in support of U.S. operations in the Middle East.

Carrier Strike Group 10

Carrier
USS George H. W. Bush (CVN-77), homeported at Naval Station Norfolk, Va.

Carrier Air Wing 7

  • The “Jolly Rogers” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 103 – F/A-18E/F – from Naval Air Station Oceana, Va.
  • The “Rampagers” of VFA 83 – F/A-18E – from Naval Air Station Oceana.
  • The “Gunslingers” of VFA 105 – F/A-18E/F – from Naval Air Station Oceana.
  • The “Wildcats” of VFA 131 – F/A-18E – Naval Air Station Oceana.
  • The “Patriots” of Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 140 – EA-18G – from Naval Air Station Whidbey Island, Wash.
  • The “Sun Kings” of Airborne Command and Control Squadron (VAW) 116 – E-2C – from Naval Air Station Point Mugu, Calif.
  • The “Mighty Bison” of Fleet Logistics Multi-Mission Squadron (VRM) 40 — CMV-22B — from Naval Air Station Norfolk, Va.
  • The “Grandmasters” of Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 46 – MH-60R – from Naval Air Station Jacksonville, Fla.
  • The “Nightdippers” of Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 5 – MH 60S — from Naval Air Station Norfolk.

Destroyer Squadron 22

Destroyer Squadron 22 is based in Naval Station Norfolk, Va., and embarked on George H.W. Bush.

  • USS Donald Cook (DDG-75), homeported at Naval Station Mayport, Fla.

Additionally, deployed warships in the region include:

  • USS Milius (DDG-69), homeported in Yokosuka, Japan.
  • USS John Paul Jones (DDG-53), homeported at Naval Station Everett, Wash.
  • USS Rafael Peralta (DDG-115), homeported in Yokosuka.
  • USS John Finn (DDG-113), homeported in Yokosuka.
  • USS Carl M. Levin (DDG-120), homeported at Naval Station Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
  • USS Mason (DDG-87), homeported at Naval Station Mayport.
  • USS Princeton (CG-59), homeported at Naval Station San Diego.
  • USS Wayne E. Meyer (DDG-108), homeported at Naval Station Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
  • USS Miguel Keith (ESB-5), homeported in Apra Harbor, Guam.

Aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) is also now operating in the Arabian Sea.

Strike Group 9 is composed of Theodore Roosevelt, Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 11, Destroyer Squadron 23, Information Warfare Squadron 9 and Ticonderoga-class guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65).

Carrier Strike Group 9

Carrier
USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), homeported at Naval Air Station, North Island, Calif.

Carrier Air Wing 11

  • The “Black Knights” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 154 – F/A-18F – from Naval Air Station Lemoore, Calif.
  • The “Checkmates” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 211 – F/A-18E – from Naval Air Station, Oceana, Va.
  • The “Fist of the Fleet” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 25 – F/A-18E – from Naval Air Station Lemoore.
  • The “Sidewinders” of Strike Fighter Squadron (VFA) 86 – F-35C– from Naval Air Station Lemoore.
  • The “Rooks” of Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 137 – EA-18G – from Naval Air Station Whidbey Island, Wash.
  • The “Liberty Bells” of Airborne Command and Control Squadron (VAW) 115 – E-2D – from Naval Air Station Point Mugu, Calif.
  • The “Titans” of Fleet Logistics Multi-Mission Squadron 30 (VRM-30) Det _ – CMV-22B – from Naval Air Station North Island, Calif.
  • The “Wolf Pack” of Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron (HSM) 75 – MH-60R – from Naval Air Station North Island.
  • The “Eightballers” of Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 8 – MH-60S – from Naval Air Station North Island.

Air Defense Commander

  • USS Chosin (CG-65), homeported at Naval Station San Diego, Calif.

Destroyer Squadron 23

Destroyer Squadron 23 is based in Naval Station San Diego, Calif., and embarked aboard Theodore Roosevelt.

  • USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60), homeported at Naval Station San Diego.
  • USS Decatur (DDG-73), homeported at Naval Station Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.

The Theodore Roosevelt CSG also deployed with Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Seahawk.

In the Indian Ocean

Amphibious assault ship USS Boxer (LHD-4) is operating in the Indian Ocean.

The Boxer Amphibious Ready Group includes Boxer, USS Comstock (LSD-45), USS Portland (LPD-27) and the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit.

USS Mustin (DDG-89), homeported in Yokosuka, Japan, is also operating in the Indian Ocean.

In the Western Atlantic

Aircraft carrier USS Nimitz (CVN-68) returned last Monday to Norfolk, Va., according to ship spotters.

In addition to these major formations, not shown are others serving in submarines, individual surface ships, aircraft squadrons, SEALs, Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Forces, Seabees, EOD Mobile Units and more throughout the globe.
